subject: Overprediction at Regions of Low Response Values

messages.author: 96e275f43eafb053
messages.subject: Overprediction at Regions of Low Response Values
parts:
Hi All,

I have fitted a geostatistical model using INLA and I am getting overpredicted estimates for regions with low values.
How can I reduce these overprediction?
Many Thanks.

Eliud

'better model' (without knowing how to do that...) ;-))

Thanks Rue. 

Let me try using non default INLA priors and see whether the overprediction reduces. 
Could be the way I am specifying non stationary (code below) lead to underprediction in high values and overprediction in the low values regionds

basis.T <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2, degree=2)
basis.K <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2,degree=2)

spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha=2,B.tau=cbind(0, basis.T, basis.K*0),
                         B.kappa=cbind(0, basis.T*0, basis.K/2))

Kibuchi

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Overprediction at Regions of Low Response Values
parts:
On Wed, 2015-04-22 at 06:21 -0700, K.e wrote:

> Let me try using non default INLA priors and see whether the
> overprediction reduces.
> Could be the way I am specifying non stationary (code below) lead to
> underprediction in high values and overprediction in the low values
> regionds

What you now describe is usually called "oversmoothing", and yes, the
priors will have an effect on this. You need to specify at least the
prior precision for the parameters, and possibly also the prior median.

Finn

>
>
> basis.T <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2, degree=2)
> basis.K <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2,degree=2)
